title: Restore a release launcher
task: Give the owner execute permission on bin/release-version, run it directly as ./bin/release-version, and save stdout as version.txt. Keep the script contents unchanged.
hints: Run ls -l bin/release-version and read its interpreter line. Compare the owner permission slots before and after chmod.

checks.label: The unchanged launcher is executable by its owner
checks.feedback: Inspect ls -l bin/release-version. chmod u+x adds the owner execute bit while preserving unrelated permissions.

checks.label: The report contains the launcher’s version output
checks.feedback: Run ./bin/release-version > version.txt from lab/, then inspect the report with cat.

demo.visual:
-rw-r--r--  bin/show-build
 owner: rw-   group: r--   others: r--
demo.explanation: The owner can read and write, but the third owner slot is missing x. A valid interpreter line alone does not make the file executable.
u selects the owner, + adds a permission, and x means execute. File contents and the other permission slots remain unchanged.
./ selects the path in the current directory. A direct run uses execute permission; > captures stdout and cat lets you inspect it.
